audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Artificial Intelligence bachelor studies intelligence in people and machines through computing, mathematics, cognitive science, language and philosophy.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The 2026–2027 example follows Utrecht’s Learning and Computation package. The three UCR plans focus on AI and cognitive science, software and autonomous systems, or reasoning and human cognition.

cellNotes.text: Both develop programming and computational problem-solving. UCR uses Python.
Both study methods for intelligent systems. UCR focuses on probabilistic decision-making under uncertainty.
Both study data structures, algorithms and computational complexity.
Both teach machine-learning methods and model evaluation. UCR covers regression, classification and unsupervised learning.
UCR studies transformers and language applications within a broader neural networks course. Utrecht provides a dedicated language models course.
UCR develops advanced learning through reinforcement learning and implementing agents. Utrecht’s course covers a broader set of advanced machine-learning methods.
Both teach mathematics for modelling. UCR focuses on calculus, equations and dynamic models.
Both develop formal logic for computing and AI. UCR also covers discrete structures and proof techniques.
Both develop statistical and experimental methods for empirical research.
Both introduce human cognition and ways to study it. UCR also gives an introduction to neuroanatomy and behaviour.
Both study language processing and how to investigate it. UCR emphasises the psychology and neuroscience of language.
Utrecht builds computational models of language processing. UCR studies language applications within deep learning and human language in psycholinguistics.
Both consider philosophical questions about intelligence and mind. UCR also studies identity and conscious experience.
Both consider philosophical questions about AI. UCR focuses on issues such as fairness, privacy, agency and responsibility.
Utrecht provides a dedicated course on formal and natural languages. UCR covers related formal tools within logic and algorithms.
Utrecht devotes a course to connections between natural processes and computation.
Utrecht provides a dedicated advanced logic course. UCR develops formal reasoning within logic and algorithms.
Utrecht requires a supervised thesis after preparation in experimental methods. UCR offers optional independent research outside these schedules.
Utrecht leaves 45 EC for profiling, such as a minor or electives, subject to programme requirements.

notes.text: Utrecht combines a common AI core with a formal depth package. UCR covers related topics across AI, mathematics, software, cognitive science and philosophy. Utrecht gives more dedicated study to formal languages, advanced logic and computational language processing.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENBUSI211.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
BENBUSI211.text: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.text: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

DISARIN211.name: Decision-making in AI
DISARIN211.text: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Students study probability, Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.

Students work with propositions, quantified statements, sets, Boolean algebra, functions and relations, direct and indirect proofs, induction and recursion. A final component models processes and games without chance and investigates winning strategies.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
